question.text: Meher Foundation CSR Trust (corporate CSR arm of a listed parent) had a CSR obligation of INR 5 crore for FY 2024-25, against an ongoing multi-year education project for Roshni Trust. It spent INR 3.8 crore during the year on the ongoing project and carried forward INR 1.2 crore to be spent over the remaining project tenure. Under Companies Act Section 135 and Rule 4(6)/7 of CSR Rules, which treatment of the unspent INR 1.2 crore is CORRECT?

answer.text: The INR 1.2 crore must be deposited in PM CARES Fund within 30 days of year-end — ongoing-project treatment is not allowed
The INR 1.2 crore lapses and cannot be carried forward under any circumstances
The INR 1.2 crore is automatically added to next year's CSR budget without any separate account requirement
The INR 1.2 crore, being attributable to an ongoing project, must be transferred to an 'Unspent CSR Account' within 30 days of year-end and utilised within 3 financial years

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 135(6) of the Companies Act 2013 requires that any unspent CSR amount pursuant to an ongoing project must be transferred to a separate 'Unspent CSR Account' (in a scheduled bank) within 30 days of the end of the financial year and must be spent within 3 financial years from the date of transfer. If not spent, the balance is transferred to a Schedule VII fund (e.g., PM CARES) within 30 days of expiry. This carry-forward is specifically permitted ONLY for ongoing projects — non-ongoing-project unspent amounts must go directly to a Schedule VII fund within 6 months of year-end. The Trap: Direct PM CARES transfer is the rule for NON-ongoing projects or for lapsed amounts after 3 years — not the first-step treatment for ongoing projects. 'Lapses' is wrong. 'Auto addition to next year' skips the separate-account and 3-year deadline entirely. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser), III-A/III-C (Compliance) test CSR mechanics. XXIII asks the SIA to correctly reflect unspent-CSR tagging in the Impact Report's funding-source table. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Ask the donor corporate for the Unspent CSR Account bank statement — not just the CSR-2 form. The reconciliation of 'committed vs disbursed vs unspent' is frequently broken at year-end and can cause double-counting across Annual Impact Reports. Disclose the Unspent CSR balance as a contingent funding line in the AIR funding annexure.
